nodes.chainStep: Airway and vital signs; repeat the BP in both arms and feel the pulses; look for acute organ damage (neurologic exam, fundi, ECG, creatinine, urine dipstick); test for pregnancy; ask about cocaine and other drugs
nodes.why: Acute organ damage, not the number, separates a hypertensive emergency from severe hypertension without it, and the kind of damage directs the drug, the target and the pace. Pressures in both arms and the pulses screen for a dissection, the fundi for hemorrhages or papilledema, the urine for blood and protein; pregnancy is excluded in a woman who could be pregnant, and drugs such as cocaine are asked about. Lowering first treats the number: without acute organ damage the pressure is not lowered aggressively or with IV drugs, and one set target is wrong for a dissection or a stroke.

nodes.chainStep: Protect the airway; non-contrast CT head before setting the BP target
nodes.why: A bleed or an infarct changes the target, and hypertensive encephalopathy is a diagnosis of exclusion, so the scan that rules out a hemorrhage comes first, before the BP plan. Lowering before the scan sets a target blind, rapid correction to normal can starve organs whose autoregulation is lost, and short-acting nifedipine is not used. nodes.why: Labetalol is contraindicated in bronchial asthma, heart block beyond first degree and severe bradycardia, and the guideline adds reactive airway or obstructive pulmonary disease; its label adds that beta blockers, even cardioselective ones, should not be used with obstructive airway disease. Hydralazine is an undesirable first-line agent because its response is unpredictable and long, and enalaprilat is slow to act (15 minutes) and unpredictable.

NICE: 4 g IV over 5 to 15 minutes, then 1 g an hour for 24 hours. StatPearls: 6 g IV over 15 to 20 minutes, then 2 g an hour
orders.note: NICE loads 4 g; StatPearls loads 6 g.

orders.dose: Maintenance fluids no more than 80 mL an hour in severe pre-eclampsia
First below 160/110, then 135/85 or less

nodes.ask: Severe hypertension, no acute organ damage, not pregnant. Plan?
options: Start or restart oral therapy; review within 7 days
IV labetalol to under 160/100, then discharge
Admit for an IV nicardipine infusion until it is normal
Sublingual nifedipine now, discharge once it has fallen
nodes.chainStep: No IV drugs and no rapid lowering; restart or step up oral therapy, or confirm a new diagnosis with a repeat or ambulatory reading; address pain and anxiety; review within 7 days
nodes.why: Without acute organ damage the pressure is not lowered aggressively or with IV drugs; oral therapy is restarted or intensified, preferably as an outpatient, and the pressure comes down over days to weeks. Rapid lowering has not been shown to help and can harm, short-acting nifedipine is not used, and admission for an infusion treats the number.

nodes.note: NICE confirms a new diagnosis before treating it; BIHS and StatPearls start or adjust oral therapy. Both fit the key.

nodes.summary: Convulsing with severe hypertension, not pregnant: stop the seizure first in the seizure pathway. Once it stops, a non-contrast CT head comes before the BP plan, as on the neurologic route here.

Intracerebral hemorrhage: smooth IV lowering to a systolic of 130 to 139 for at least 7 days when it starts at 150 to 220, never below 130 (AHA/ACC; BIHS aims for 140 to 180, and 140 or more above 220). Continue in the stroke pathway for anticoagulant reversal, the hematoma site and surgery.

Subarachnoid hemorrhage: continue in the headache pathway for CT angiography, nimodipine and securing the aneurysm. Its blood pressure target is not settled in the sources read; BIHS lowers it only for a compelling reason, with a titratable agent, to 140 to 180/90 to 110.
A subdural or a mass explains the picture, so this is not hypertensive encephalopathy. Treating the lesion, and the pressure that goes with it, is outside this pathway's sources.

Ischemic stroke with a lytic: below 185/110 before it and under 180/105 for 24 hours after; 180/105 or less during and for 24 hours after any thrombectomy. Continue in the stroke pathway for the lytic, its dose and thrombectomy.
Ischemic stroke going to thrombectomy without a lytic: 180/105 or less during and for 24 hours after the procedure. Continue in the stroke pathway for thrombectomy.

Ischemic stroke without reperfusion: leave the pressure alone under 220/120; at 220/120 or more, lower it by about 15% over the first day. Continue in the stroke pathway for antiplatelets and imaging.

Hypertensive emergency without a compelling condition: ICU and an arterial line, a titratable IV agent, systolic down by no more than 25% in the first hour, under 160/100 over 2 to 6 hours, then cautiously to 130 to 140 over 24 to 48 hours, then oral therapy. Nicardipine or clevidipine when a beta blocker is ruled out.

Type A dissection: emergency surgical consultation and immediate surgery; meanwhile beta blocker first, systolic 120 or less, heart rate 60 to 80 (aortic guideline; BIHS 60 or less); transfer to a high-volume aortic center if stable enough. The chest pain pathway carries the same route.
Type B dissection: medical therapy first when uncomplicated (ICU, beta blocker, systolic under 120, heart rate 60 to 80, or 60 or less in BIHS); intervention for rupture or other complications.

No aortic syndrome on CT angiography: the dissection targets lapse. Back to the organ damage screen: an ECG and troponin for ACS (chest pain pathway); with no acute organ damage, it is severe hypertension, lowered slowly by mouth.

ACS with severe hypertension: IV nitroglycerin (not after a PDE-5 inhibitor or with an RV infarct) and esmolol if there is no beta-blocker contraindication; mean pressure down 20 to 25% at most, diastolic 70 or more, no nitroprusside; revascularization first. Continue in the chest pain pathway.
Hypertensive pulmonary edema: IV nitroglycerin, clevidipine or nitroprusside with an IV loop diuretic; no beta blocker; mean pressure down 25% at most. Breathing support sits in the dyspnea pathway.

Cocaine or amphetamine hypertension: IV benzodiazepines first, titrated until calm, with cooling if hot; if the pressure stays high, IV phentolamine or nitroglycerin (BIHS adds IV nicardipine or a labetalol infusion; both are disputed); no beta blocker alone, no short-acting nifedipine; with ischemic chest pain, IV nitroglycerin and the chest pain pathway.

Pheochromocytoma crisis: IV phentolamine (or nicardipine or clevidipine) and IV fluids, no beta blocker until alpha blockade is in place; confirm with metanephrines, then oral alpha blockade before surgery.

Eclampsia: IV magnesium sulfate, 4 g over 5 to 15 minutes, then 1 g an hour until 24 hours after the last fit (StatPearls loads 6 g, then 2 g an hour), 2 to 4 g more for a recurrent fit, never diazepam or phenytoin in its place; treat the severe pressure at once with labetalol, oral nifedipine or IV hydralazine. Continue in the seizure pathway.

Severe-range pressure in pregnancy: labetalol, oral nifedipine or IV hydralazine now, first to below 160/110; magnesium sulfate when severe features are present; no ACE inhibitor, ARB or nitroprusside before birth. The obstetric team decides on timing of birth (headache and seizure pathways).

Pregnant or recently delivered with a focal deficit or a GCS below 13: protect the airway and get a non-contrast CT head; treat a severe-range pressure at once with labetalol, oral nifedipine or IV hydralazine, and give magnesium if this may be eclampsia. The rest is outside this pathway's sources.
Not yet severe hypertension without organ damage: continue in the chest pain or headache pathway; no IV lowering for the number alone.

Severe hypertension without acute organ damage: no IV drugs and no rapid lowering; restart or step up oral therapy, or confirm a new diagnosis, and review within 7 days. No short-acting nifedipine, and no as-needed doses for a ward patient.

cases.label: Unresponsive, intracerebral hemorrhage
cases.vignette: 71-year-old man found slumped in his chair by his daughter; he takes amlodipine and lisinopril. BP 214/122, HR 64, SpO2 94%, glucose 6.4 mmol/L (115 mg/dL).

results.front: GCS 9 (E2 V2 M5), snoring respirations, not convulsing.
results.neuro_ct: Non-contrast CT: a left basal ganglia hemorrhage.

cases.label: Hypertensive encephalopathy
cases.vignette: 44-year-old man who stopped his blood pressure tablets a month ago, 2 days of worsening headache and vomiting, now muddled. BP 238/136, HR 96, afebrile.

results.front: Both arms 238/136. GCS 14, disoriented to the date, no focal deficit; flame hemorrhages and disc swelling in both fundi. ECG: LVH, no ischemic change.
results.neuro_ct: Non-contrast CT: no bleed or infarct; patchy low density in both occipital lobes.
results.agent_limits: No asthma, no heart block, no allergies; HR 96.

cases.label: Malignant hypertension with kidney injury, asthma
cases.vignette: 36-year-old woman, a week of headache and passing less urine. BP 226/134, HR 88.

results.front: Both arms 226/134. Alert and oriented, normal neurologic exam; retinal hemorrhages and cotton wool spots in both eyes. Creatinine 3.1 mg/dL (274 micromol/L), 0.9 six months ago; urine 2+ blood, 2+ protein. Pregnancy test negative. ECG: no ischemic change.
results.agent_limits: Asthma since childhood, on an inhaled steroid and salbutamol.

cases.label: Ischemic stroke, reperfusion planned
cases.vignette: 66-year-old woman, sudden right arm weakness and slurred speech 90 minutes ago; not on an anticoagulant. BP 204/112, HR 82 and irregular, glucose normal.

results.front: GCS 15; right face and arm weakness, expressive aphasia. Fundi normal. ECG: atrial fibrillation, no ischemic change.
results.neuro_ct: Non-contrast CT: no bleed, no established infarct.
results.ais_elig: Stroke team: within 4.5 hours, no contraindication; a lytic and CT angiography for thrombectomy are planned.

cases.label: Ischemic stroke, thrombectomy without a lytic
cases.vignette: 58-year-old man, sudden left-sided weakness and his eyes turned to the right 3 hours ago; he takes apixaban, last dose this morning. BP 192/106, HR 88 and irregular.

results.front: GCS 14; dense left hemiparesis, gaze deviation to the right. Fundi normal. ECG: atrial fibrillation, no ischemic change.
results.neuro_ct: Non-contrast CT: no bleed; a hyperdense right middle cerebral artery.
results.ais_elig: Stroke team: apixaban this morning rules out the lytic; CT angiography shows a right M1 occlusion; thrombectomy planned.

cases.label: Ischemic stroke, no reperfusion
cases.vignette: 79-year-old man who woke with a weak left side; last seen well 16 hours ago. BP 198/108, HR 76.

results.front: GCS 15; left face, arm and leg weakness, a left visual field loss. Fundi normal.
results.neuro_ct: Non-contrast CT: no bleed; early low density in the right MCA territory.
results.ais_elig: Stroke team: outside the lytic window, no large vessel occlusion on CT angiography; no lytic or thrombectomy.

cases.label: Subarachnoid hemorrhage with severe hypertension
cases.vignette: 52-year-old woman, a sudden severe headache while lifting a box, then vomiting. BP 206/116, HR 58.

results.front: GCS 14, confused, neck stiff, no focal deficit. Fundi: no papilledema. Pregnancy test negative.
results.neuro_ct: Non-contrast CT: blood in the basal cisterns and both sylvian fissures.

cases.label: Subdural, not encephalopathy
cases.vignette: 83-year-old man on aspirin, a week of headache and growing confusion. BP 192/104, HR 70.

results.front: GCS 14, drowsy and disoriented, no focal deficit; fundi normal.
results.neuro_ct: Non-contrast CT: a left convexity subdural hematoma with midline shift.

cases.label: Type A dissection
cases.vignette: 61-year-old man with hypertension, sudden severe chest pain that goes through to his back. HR 104.

results.front: Right arm 212/118, left arm 168/96; a faint left radial pulse. ECG: sinus tachycardia, no ST elevation. Neurologic exam normal.
results.cta: CT angiography: an intimal flap from the aortic root into the arch.

cases.label: Type B dissection
cases.vignette: 68-year-old woman, sudden tearing pain between the shoulder blades. HR 98.

results.front: Right arm 208/112, left arm 204/110; the left femoral pulse is weaker than the right. ECG: sinus rhythm, no ST elevation.
results.cta: CT angiography: a flap starting beyond the left subclavian artery; the ascending aorta is spared; no rupture, kidneys and bowel perfused.

cases.label: Suspected dissection, CT angiography clear
cases.vignette: 55-year-old man, sudden sharp chest pain spreading to his back while lifting weights. HR 92.

results.front: Right arm 196/110, left arm 172/98; leg pulses equal. ECG: LVH with strain, no ST elevation. Neurologic exam normal.
results.cta: CT angiography: normal aorta; no flap, hematoma or ulcer.

cases.label: ACS with severe hypertension
cases.vignette: 64-year-old man with diabetes, an hour of crushing central chest pressure. HR 92, SpO2 97%. No sildenafil or tadalafil.

results.front: Both arms 198/114, pulses equal, no back pain. ECG: 2 mm ST depression in V4 to V6. Chest clear, no edema. Neurologic exam normal.

cases.label: Hypertensive pulmonary edema
cases.vignette: 72-year-old woman, woke breathless and cannot lie flat. HR 112, SpO2 88% on air.

results.front: Both arms 224/126. Crackles to both mid zones; chest film: bilateral alveolar edema. ECG: LVH, no acute ischemic change. Alert, neurologic exam normal.

cases.label: Cocaine, settles on benzodiazepines
cases.vignette: 27-year-old man brought in by friends from a club, shouting and pacing. HR 132, temperature 37.9.

results.front: BP 210/118 in both arms. Pupils 7 mm, skin wet; friends say he snorted cocaine an hour ago. No chest pain; ECG: sinus tachycardia, no ischemic change. Neurologic exam normal apart from agitation.
results.coc_resp: After two doses of IV lorazepam: calm, BP 162/94, HR 104.

cases.label: Cocaine with ST depression
cases.vignette: 45-year-old man, an hour of chest tightness, restless and sweating. HR 124, temperature 37.4.

results.front: BP 206/120 in both arms, pulses equal, no back pain. Pupils 6 mm; he smoked crack cocaine an hour ago. ECG: 1 mm ST depression in V4 to V6. Lungs clear, neurologic exam normal.
results.coc_resp: After IV lorazepam and IV nitroglycerin: calm, BP 158/92, HR 98, the tightness easing.

cases.label: Methamphetamine, pressure stays high
cases.vignette: 34-year-old woman brought in restless and tremulous after a night awake. HR 126, temperature 37.6.

results.front: BP 218/124 in both arms. Pupils dilated, sweating; she admits smoking methamphetamine 2 hours ago. No chest pain; ECG: sinus tachycardia, no ischemic change. Pregnancy test negative.
results.coc_resp: After repeated IV diazepam: calmer, HR 110, but BP 204/118.

cases.label: Pheochromocytoma crisis
cases.vignette: 41-year-old woman, a pounding headache with palpitations for the last hour; pale and tremulous. HR 128.

results.front: BP 236/128 in both arms. Spells like this for 6 months, each with sweating; a 4 cm right adrenal mass on a CT for back pain in the spring. No drugs taken; urine drug screen and pregnancy test negative. ECG: sinus tachycardia, no ischemic change.

cases.label: Eclampsia
cases.vignette: 29-year-old woman, 35 weeks into her first pregnancy, a severe headache and flashing lights since lunchtime.

results.front: BP 184/122; 3+ protein on dipstick; no focal deficit, no chest or back pain.
results.preg_fit: A generalized tonic-clonic seizure in the bay, lasting 2 minutes.

cases.label: Pre-eclampsia, severe-range pressure
cases.vignette: 33-year-old woman, 34 weeks pregnant, a headache and spots before her eyes since this morning.

results.front: BP 186/120; 2+ protein on dipstick; no focal deficit, no chest or back pain.

cases.label: Recently delivered, GCS below 13
cases.vignette: 31-year-old woman, 6 days after a vaginal delivery, a day of headache; her partner found her hard to wake. BP 194/124, HR 96.

results.front: GCS 11, not convulsing; no focal deficit; arm pressures equal, no chest or back pain.

cases.label: Chest pain, screen clear
cases.vignette: 50-year-old man, an hour of central chest tightness, now easing. BP 192/108, HR 84.

results.front: Both arms 190/106, pulses equal, no back pain. ECG normal; first high-sensitivity troponin below the 99th percentile. Neurologic exam and fundi normal; creatinine and urine normal.

cases.label: Severe hypertension, no organ damage
cases.vignette: 58-year-old man sent from clinic with BP 196/116 twice; he ran out of amlodipine and lisinopril 10 days ago and feels well.

results.front: Repeat 194/118 in both arms. Alert, normal neurologic exam and fundi; no chest pain or breathlessness. ECG: LVH, no ischemic change. Creatinine at his baseline; urine dipstick normal.

cases.label: Convulsing with severe hypertension
cases.vignette: 38-year-old man, 3 days of headache and blurred vision, brought in after collapsing at home. BP 232/132, HR 110.

results.front: A generalized tonic-clonic seizure starts in the bay and is still going at 5 minutes; glucose 5.8 mmol/L (104 mg/dL).
